THE INTENDED WORKFLOW

Fund the order.
Prove the work. Deliver the result.

A customer orders an AI-assisted catalog cleanup. The contract specifies accepted records, budget, recipient, and dispute rules. Metering records the work; a customer-approved validator accepts the cleaned catalog. An eligible future payment adapter releases the funded USDC. Confirmed payment enables the result download, while an optional payout provider converts funds to bank money for an eligible recipient.

This is the proposed product flow, not a record of an executed order. A signature on caller-supplied observations does not make those observations independent or authenticated.

01 / MEASURE

Quantify the work.

Record the agreed unit, price, input and output evidence, provider, and execution limits. Tokens or GPU time measure resources; the buyer decides what result is worth paying for.

02 / ACCEPT & PAY

Release funded value.

The planned smart-contract layer checks accepted results and spending authority before releasing a buyer’s existing stablecoins. Reserve-backed currency needs external funding.

03 / SETTLE

Confirm the payment.

Track the approved token, network, recipient, and transaction. Redemption into bank money uses an eligible provider and its fees, controls, and terms.

04 / DELIVER

Make value useful.

Unlock an API result, fulfill an order, or deliver a service. Show the end user what was completed, what was paid, and the supporting receipt.

Build on what exists.

The public rc20 verifier checks authority policies and signs evidence. The control plane manages authorized internal records. Inspect the exact release and its limits.

Inspect the live build ↗

Validate the payment boundary.

A production contract needs authenticated metering, an acceptance authority, prefunded balances, approved token/network bindings, replay protection, a dispute path, and independent settlement reconciliation.
